newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses weak despite BT deal, dlr steady.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses weak despite BT deal, dlr steady.

text.p: European bourses were flat or weaker on Monday, with London down several points despite a jump in British Telecom shares after the surprise weekend news of its planned $20 billion merger with America's MCI Communications.

On the currency markets, the dollar was steady against the mark and yen after earlier drifting gradually down towards 113 yen. Dealers predicted it would struggle to make any gains ahead of Tuesday's U.S. presidential elections.
In New York leading Wall Street stocks were flat in early trading, having little effect on European bourses.
The London stock market was near the day's lows in the European afternoon as euphoria about telecom merger plan failed to spill over into the broad market.
The FTSE 100 share index was down five points at 3,943.5 with losers outnumbering gainers three to one.

Investors focused on the telecoms sector, which accounted for just short of one third of market volume of 320 million shares. BT led volumes and was among the top gainers after the MCI deal, the biggest transatlantic deal in history. By 1500 GMT BT shares were at 375 pence, down from the day's high of 386 but still eight pence up on the day.

Traders said business was cautious ahead of the U.S. elections and as domestic political worries revived after the death at the weekend of a Conservative MP reduced the ruling party's majority to one.
British M0 money supply and official reserves figures made little impact on either the government bond or equities markets and no major companies reported on Monday.

The FTSE closed last week at its lowest level for a month and dealers said the market remained pre-occupied over further interest rate rises after last week's unanticipated quarter percentage point tightening of monetary policy.

"As well as interest rate worries, there are anxieties about Clinton winning both houses in the U.S. elections and the impact that may have on, for instance, drug stocks in any overhaul of the healthcare system," said one head of trading.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended bourse trade down but slightly off the day's lows. Dealers said the market had been catching up with profit-taking during late Friday's electronic dealings. The 30-share DAX index ended down 11.39 points at 2,671.86. One bright spot was mixed utility Viag AG, BT's partner in Germany. Its shares rose on news of the BT/MCI merger plan.

In Paris too the mood was negative and French shares were flat after starting with modest losses, shadowing a downward drift in bond markets. Traders said operators were marking time ahead of the U.S. poll and little action was expected.

Meanwhile, the dollar tiptoed lower against the yen during the European morning as nerves were gnawed ahead of the U.S. poll, but activity was minimal and traders said tight ranges were the order of the day.

The re-election of President Bill Clinton was seen as a foregone conclusion, but the market feared the Democrats could wrest control of Congress from the Republicans and loosen trade and fiscal policy.

"The market's cautious ahead of the elections and there are lingering fears the Democrats are going to get a clean sweep -- though I think those fears are overdone," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International in London.
Trading was further subdued overnight by a Japanese holiday.
Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank, said market jitters over the outcome of the U.S. vote meant the immediate risks for the dollar were to the downside.
"Concerns remain that in the event of a Democrat clean sweep protectionist influences will come back to the fore," he said.
Last Friday's comments by former U.S. treasury secretary Lloyd Bentsen highlighted that risk, Fox said.

Bentsen told Reuters Financial Television he was comfortable with the dollar's current exchange rate but would prefer not to see dollar/yen rise further. Substantial appreciation from here would put the U.S. at a competitive disadvantage, he said.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5121 marks and 113.30 yen compared with late Friday's 1.5183 marks and 113.40 yen. STOCKS MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares had fallen 5.0 points to 3,943.5.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 2.2 points at 2,142.7.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt ended down 11.39 at 2,671.86.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $378.70 compared with 377.65 at the London close on Friday. Silver was up seven cents at $4.83.
